transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Since I stopped working, I’m struggling with how to handle this change, and my reactions are keeping me from settling into a new routine. I retired from my engineering career about six months ago, and this transition has turned out to be much more disorienting than I expected.

Since these difficulties started after retirement, have your symptoms been causing you significant distress or making it hard to function in daily life, or do they feel more like a normal adjustment that is gradually improving?

It has definitely been impacting my daily life, as I've been declining social invitations and postponing trips, which has really thinned out my social calendar. However, I do believe this is a temporary hurdle rather than a long-term problem. I expect that once I can establish a clearer routine, especially when the new STEM mentoring program restarts, these unsettled feelings will gradually improve.
Have these feelings and difficulties lasted less than 6 months, or have they continued longer than that?

They have definitely lasted less than six months; these struggles have only been going on for about the last two months since the initial excitement of retirement wore off. I fully expect this unsettled feeling to fade once I get a clearer routine established.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or felt so hopeless that you can’t cope with daily life?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, nor do I feel completely hopeless. While I do feel quite unsettled, disoriented, and disappointed in my lack of routine right now, I definitely don't want to harm myself. I still fully expect to get back on track once I find my footing in this new phase of life.
Have these difficulties started specifically after the retirement change, and are they clearly more severe than what you would expect from a normal adjustment to that life event?

Yes, they definitely started after I retired, specifically about two months after leaving the firm once the initial excitement wore off. It feels like more than a normal adjustment because I'm getting paralyzed by simple daily choices and actively avoiding activities and social invitations I used to love.
Have these adjustment difficulties continued for more than 6 months after the retirement change, or are they still within the first 6 months?

They are definitely still within that first six-month window. Although I retired six months ago, I was doing fine initially, and these difficulties only started about two months ago. So the actual struggles themselves have not been going on for very long.
Have you also been feeling persistently sad, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or having major changes in sleep or appetite since this started?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite. Also, while I am putting off activities I used to enjoy, it feels more like being stuck, unsettled, and paralyzed by simple decisions rather than feeling persistently sad.

Have these retirement-related difficulties caused you to miss work-like responsibilities, withdraw from important relationships, or otherwise interfere with your day-to-day functioning more than you would expect from a normal adjustment?

Yes, they certainly have interfered with my life and relationships. My wife has pointed out that I keep declining social invitations and postponing trips we had planned, which has really thinned out our social calendar. I've also been putting off volunteer commitments, so I'm not following through on the meaningful projects I wanted to do in retirement.
Have you been feeling a lot of excessive worry, nervousness, or physical tension about the retirement change, or is it more that you feel stuck and unable to adjust?

It is definitely more of a feeling of being "stuck" and unable to adjust, rather than feeling intensely nervous or physically tense. I feel unmoored and paralyzed by simple daily choices, which leads to me pacing, over-planning, and putting off my activities rather than feeling actively anxious or panicked. It's just a strange inability to move forward with the plans I made.
Did these difficulties begin within 3 months of the retirement change, and are they directly tied to that specific life event?

Yes, they started about two months after I retired, which is right within that three-month window. The first few weeks felt like a nice, welcome break, but once the lack of structure caught up with me, it became clear these feelings are directly tied to leaving my engineering career.
Have these adjustment difficulties improved at all since they started, or have they stayed the same or gotten worse over time?

They have stayed fairly consistent over the last two months since they first started, and I haven't really seen much improvement yet. However, I don't feel like they are getting worse, and I fully expect these unsettled feelings to fade once I can establish a clearer routine.

Since these retirement-related difficulties began, have you felt persistently down or lost interest/pleasure in most things nearly every day, or is it mainly the feeling of being stuck and unable to adjust?

It is definitely the feeling of being stuck and unable to adjust to the lack of routine rather than a persistent depression. I still have the desire and interest to do things like hiking or traveling, but I get paralyzed by simple daily choices and end up putting them off. This just leaves me feeling quite unsettled and disappointed in myself most days.
Have you had any panic attacks, constant excessive worry, or felt persistently depressed or hopeless nearly every day since this started?

No, I haven't experienced panic attacks, constant worry, or felt persistently depressed or hopeless. My experience is more about feeling unsettled, unmoored, and disappointed in myself for failing to stick to my plans. It doesn't feel like severe anxiety or deep depression, just a struggle to adjust.
Have you had any symptoms like intrusive memories, nightmares, or feeling constantly on edge related to the retirement change, or is it mainly the difficulty adjusting to the life transition?

No, I haven't had any nightmares, intrusive memories, or felt constantly on edge at all. My struggle is entirely about the difficulty adjusting to this retirement transition and feeling unmoored. I just find myself paralyzed by simple daily choices rather than experiencing those kinds of intense symptoms.
